author: Al3cs
text:
One thing I learned from Mertch is that he doesn't set stoplosses wider than 10 pips.

So if the DM level is more than 10 pips up from QM level where he took the trade, he accept the 10 pips loss and take another trade at DM level (if there's PA).

He is a disciplined money manager and a killer trader.

Please forgive me for invading into your journal. I have spent some times looking at your charts, and I have few questions regarding the way you draw FLs. I know you prefer to give short answers, so I am going to write my questions in such a way that you need only answer "YES" or "NO".

Second question is to do with a statement that you made which gave me 'AHA' moment, pourriez-vous confirmer ma comprehension SVP? This is what you wrote:

When I see piece of PA inside a flag, then for me it became LIMIT

This is my understanding:

"we know that if we draw every FL we see on the chart, it will be unreadable. So we have to choose the important ones. How do we pick the importance ones? We wait for price to come back to the FL and look at the reaction. If price makes PA (FO, QM or DM) inside the FL and then get rejected away (meaning the FL manages to hold price), then we know this FL is an important one, and we can consider looking for a trade here in the future.."

About FL,

Yes you're right, we could draw FL for ever if we'd draw them all. Whitch ones are important to me? The ones that limit the price at important levels. What are important levels? The answer is subjective. I guess IF would give you a better advise on them. For myself, I take highs, lows, break points on a given TF and I draw lines. I look what kind of reaction I have around them. Do they print CP, FL, highs or lows. I'm giving you an exemple on this quick chart;

UCAD, at that time, was inside a CP zone, breaking highs and lows, making ups and downs. I'd say I would have choose B as a price continuation and look on the other side for PA down. It never happen that way.

For the 2nd chart, I'm still ok the way I've drew my FL. The price break 1 but the FL limit the price to go lower from 1 to the lowest point. I see 1 is engulf by price momentum, comeback in and go back to engulf FL around 7657. The price comeback to my FL and print PA (3) to go higher. So maybe I've broke the rules but I don't see how I did it.

J'espère avoir répondu à tes questions!

author: Astrokillah
text:
Oui Maître! Vous avez été très généreux

Regarding the FL on AUDUSD, I knew I was just being too 'nail picking'. If we follow the rule it was candle 1 that broke the 'local resistance' and price retraced to the low of candle 2 before it went up. At the end if didn't matter because price did come back and touch this FL at 3.

I was trying to be too mechanical and precise - and sometimes that can be dangerous. We trade 1 min data, and sometimes bad data from brokers (a spike here and there) can mess up our analysis.

Je voulais vous remercier pour votre gentillesse

AK

text:
Comdemned to fail

Hello everyone,

I want to show you mistake I've made with audusd on a previous post I've made about FL. The trade I took on aud was a bit lucky (200pips run) . What I taught a FL DM trade was actualy an engulf of a FL. I was really surprise on looking at it but I didn't want to do the same mistake twice and I want to share it with you. The level was comdemned to fail on return. If I was a bit aware at that time, I could have had a good trade short with aud, But I was lucky enough to get the eurusd short and stay on it at what we could think to be a valid FL. Sorry guys, I hope you'll understand my mixt of Fren-glish
